goal: Understand SQL window functions well enough to rewrite my self-join reports
interpretation: After 30 minutes of watching, the learner can read and write PostgreSQL window functions (OVER, PARTITION BY, ranking, LAG/LEAD, running totals) and confidently replace their self-join based reports with them.
assumptions: Self-join reports are typically things like previous-row comparisons, running totals, and top-N per group, so the plan targets those patterns.
'No full SQL courses' means the learner wants short, focused videos rather than long multi-hour course uploads.
PostgreSQL syntax is preferred, but examples in other SQL dialects are acceptable since window function syntax is largely standard.

sub_topics.title: OVER() and PARTITION BY: how window functions differ from GROUP BY
sub_topics.why: The learner knows GROUP BY aggregates well, so the key shift is keeping row-level detail while computing per-group values.

sub_topics.title: ROW_NUMBER, RANK, DENSE_RANK with ORDER BY inside OVER
sub_topics.why: Replaces self-joins and correlated subqueries used for top-N per group and de-duplication.

sub_topics.title: LAG and LEAD for previous/next row comparisons
sub_topics.why: Self-joins on id-1 or date-1 for period-over-period reports are exactly what LAG/LEAD replace.

sub_topics.title: Running totals and window frames (ROWS BETWEEN, default frame behavior)
sub_topics.why: Cumulative sums and moving averages are usually done with self-joins on <= conditions; frames make this simple and fast.

sub_topics.title: Rewriting self-join reports with window functions in PostgreSQL
sub_topics.why: Ties the pieces together by converting real self-join queries into window function versions, which is the learner's actual goal.
